overview: A one-page Department of State list of papers concerning automobiles in Japan, indexing two February–March 1940 records. The first concerns the temporary shutdown of the Ford Motor Company of Japan and tentative cooperation with Japanese interests; the second concerns Count Aisuke Kabayama’s planned visit to the United States to contact an engineering institute in Pittsburgh and the Ford company regarding Japan’s motor-car industry.

subfiles.title: Department of State list of papers concerning automobiles in Japan
subfiles.about: The sheet indexes two 1940 reports concerning Ford’s Japanese operations and Count Aisuke Kabayama’s automobile-industry contacts in the United States.
subfiles.summary: Entry 43 identifies a February 23, 1940, report from Yokohama by Boyce on the temporary shutdown of the Ford Motor Company of Japan and tentative cooperation with Japanese interests. Entry 44 identifies a March 6 report from Japan by Grew concerning Count Aisuke Kabayama’s proposed visit to the United States. Kabayama intended to contact an engineering institute in Pittsburgh and the Ford company in connection with Japan’s motor-car industry.

interest: This sheet is useful as a compact roadmap to two diplomatic reports on the Japanese automobile industry in early 1940. It links Ford’s operational difficulties in Japan with elite efforts to cultivate American engineering and corporate contacts through Count Aisuke Kabayama, illustrating the persistence of industrial exchange shortly before the final deterioration of U.S.–Japanese relations.
